A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MPO research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison despite appendix expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Kuhn Poker experiments, Gemma safety-alignment results, and general-capability evaluations of trained language models, including additional appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds PPO and Iterative DPO comparisons and evaluation of a trained Llama-3-8B reward model.

M1.justification: The written MPO and MPO-RT objectives change the response expectation from the frozen iterate to the optimized policy, correcting the advantage term's policy dependence (v1 Eqs. 6–8; v2 Eqs. 7–9). The core MMD update, periodic magnet replacement, and architectures remain unchanged; these corrections do not establish that experimental implementations changed.

E1.justification: v2 removes the MT-bench two-turn dialogue evaluation reported in v1 Appendix D.2 and Table 10. Safety datasets, MixEval/MixEval-Hard, Open LLM Leaderboard v2, and RewardBench remain. The new baseline experiments reuse existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix D.1 and Figure 7 add PPO and Iterative DPO with Best-of-4 and Best-of-8 sampling to the Llama-3 MixEval-Hard comparison. This substantially extends comparison beyond SFT and MPO iterations. PPO's existing participation in the separate Kuhn Poker experiment does not make its LLM comparison pre-existing.

E3.justification: The added baseline comparison introduces matched SFT/data controls, reward-model training on the preference-model corpus, and Best-of-4/Best-of-8 sampling settings. PPO receives specified learning rates, batch size, sequence length, and pretraining-loss settings. Existing MPO training settings in Tables 4, 6, and 7 are retained.

E4.justification: The new Best-of-4 versus Best-of-8 curves examine Iterative DPO's sensitivity to response sampling. The MT-bench breakdown examining performance across dialogue turns is removed. Existing self-play, fixed-reference, clipping, and MPO-RT analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. The added comparator curves retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Figure 7 reports MPO finishing above PPO and both Iterative DPO configurations; new Table 9 reports Llama-3-8B-RM RewardBench results. Conversely, v1's MT-bench result table is removed. These substantially change the comparative evidence, although retained MPO scores—including the 44.2 final MixEval-Hard score—are unchanged. Preference-model RewardBench changes are equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: v2 adds equilibrium-uniqueness and optimality proofs in Lemmas E.1 and E.4, revises the proofs of Lemma 3.3 and Theorem 3.4, and corrects the latter proof's sign from positive to negative. New Lemmas F.2–F.3 and Theorem F.4 introduce approximate-subgame analysis and a claimed O(1/sqrt(N)) duality-gap bound under additional smoothness assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: original-game last-iterate convergence, efficient alignment using the final model, and improved LLM performance. Added comparisons and theoretical analysis support existing claims without redefining their stated scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking Iterative DPO performance to on-policy sampling and negative gradients, and discusses the quality/computation tradeoff of Best-of-N sampling. Section 3.2 also clarifies compatibility with other last-iterate subgame solvers. The MT-bench discussion identifying difficulty maintaining performance across dialogue turns is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds baseline implementation provenance through Safe-RLHF and OpenRLHF, reward-model data reuse, and concrete PPO hyperparameters, including actor learning rate 5e-7, critic learning rate 9e-6, batch size 64, and maximum length 1024. Existing MPO implementation, hardware, and training disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Theorem 3.2 is now explicitly attributed as adapted from Sokota et al. New references support equilibrium proofs, convergence-rate analysis, OpenRLHF, and sampling interpretations; the MT-bench reference is removed. The main related-work section and central research positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include title and affiliation edits, localized language and notation corrections, expanded proof explanations, and reordering Appendix D so MPO precedes MPO-RT. The main narrative and section organization are substantially retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the baseline comparison figure and reward-model table, removes the MT-bench table, and relocates several displays. Appendix bar charts receive new colors and corrected Gemma model legends; the retained MPO/MPO-RT curve loses numerical point annotations. These are limited display revisions within the existing visual structure.

improvement.justification: The new PPO/Iterative DPO comparison improves empirical context, while corrected objective expressions, proof signs, and explicit attribution improve precision. These gains are tempered by removing MT-bench's multi-turn evidence. Theorem F.4's proof specializes to a Euclidean mirror map and requires approximation accuracy not clearly connected to the implemented KL updates, so the expanded theory does not clearly resolve the practical convergence gap.
